headline: The shorter wall limits the water
statement: Choose two vertical lines from height. Their horizontal distance times the smaller height is the water area. Return the largest area; lines cannot be tilted.
prerequisites: Area as width times limiting height
intuition: Two lines form the sides of a container. Its area is their distance multiplied by the shorter height. Start with the widest pair. After measuring it, move the shorter side inward: keeping that short side and reducing the width cannot give a larger area.
approach: Start left at 0 and right at the last index.
Advance the pointer at the shorter wall, repeating until pointers meet.
correctness: If height[left] <= height[right], every pair using left and an interior right has no greater height limit and a smaller width. Discarding left loses no better pair. The symmetric argument handles right; the best measured pair is therefore best possible.
bruteForce: List every pair of walls in O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); additional space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Use the shorter height, not the larger.
Width is the index difference, not the number of intervening cells.
Move only a shorter side; either side works on a tie.
